config.text: Studio product photograph, top-down, of one single tall narrow vertical menu card, proportion 10 by 21 centimetres, thick uncoated deep burgundy cotton paper, colour #560002, lying flat and centred on a pale warm grey linen cloth, soft even daylight, the whole card visible with a margin of linen around it. The only printing is hot-foil stamping in two flat layers: a fish in matte white foil underneath, a lamb in bright silver foil on top, opaque where they overlap. Each foil is one uniform solid area with crisp sharp edges and a slight debossed relief in the paper. The motif is a small stamp placed in the centre of the card: the whole motif fits inside a zone about one third of the card's width. All the rest of the card, above, below and on both sides, is empty plain burgundy paper. No lettering, no border, no frame, no stars, no leaves, no other ornament anywhere on the card. Drawing style: the bold graphic language of a linocut or a woodcut, redrawn as clean sharp shapes: strong flat silhouettes, angular confident contours, and a few thick cut lines inside the shapes for the fleece, the scales and the fins. No carving texture, no gouge marks, no ink speckles, no hatching, no fine detail, nothing smooth or airbrushed. Simple, sharp and legible at small size. The lamb has short drooping ears and a lamb's short muzzle. Both faces are calm and neutral, mouths closed, a simple eye. The two animals are intertwined: their bodies cross and pass over and under each other. Composition: the fish's long body curves in an S around a rearing lamb, passing in front of the lamb's chest and behind its hind legs; the two heads face each other at the top.
